newsitem.title: UK: EMI warns on sterling, U.S. market recovers.
newsitem.headline: EMI warns on sterling, U.S. market recovers.

text.p: British music and publishing company EMI Group Plc, which earlier forecast the strong pound would cut profits by 30 million pounds ($50.2 million) in the current year, said on Friday it now expected a hit of between 45 million and 50 million stg.

The company said its markets in Japan and France remained less than favourable but the U.S. was showing signs of recovery and EMI's market share there was back to just under 13 percent from 10 percent previously.
In its statement to the annual shareholder meeting, EMI said it expected to save up to 23.5 million pounds in tax by paying its final dividend for 1997 as a foreign income dividend (FID).
EMI said growth in the global music market was slowing and Britain was unlikely to improve.
But it said it was still confident for the long term and predicted a recovery in the coming years in established markets and continued rapid growth in many developing markets.

The company said efforts to combat music piracy were having an effect. EMI said the annual cost of piracy was now estimated at around $2.0 billion, or five percent of the market. At the beginning of the 1990s, the pirate market took closer to six percent of the total, EMI said.
